tools.name: dig
tools.description: Ask a public DNS resolver, or any public address, for a record, live, from the isitdns seat. Returns the answer, the flags, the rcode, Extended DNS Errors and the latency in the shape dig prints, plus the JSON.

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: The eleven-check DNS audit for a domain: parent and child nameservers agree, no open recursion, DNSSEC chain, TTL sanity, mail posture, glue at the parent, a DS that matches a live DNSKEY, and whether a truncated UDP answer can be had over TCP. Every check reports ok, warn, fail or skipped with the

tools.name: trace
tools.description: Walk the delegation from the root servers down to the authoritative server for a name, like dig +trace, and say in plain steps whether the delegation is healthy.

tools.name: resolver_status
tools.description: The live board: is public DNS OK right now? Every public resolver isitdns watches, its latest reading (status, latency, DNSSEC), read every 3 minutes over DoT, with the time it was read. Give a resolver to get one card.

tools.name: resolver_history
tools.description: The incident record for the public resolvers: start time, duration and severity of each. Notable incidents by default; all=true includes short degradations. Windows where several operators failed at once are excluded as our own seat's path, and the answer says how many.

tools.name: top_domains
tools.description: The DNS health of the top 100 domains as of the last DAILY snapshot: rcode, addresses, DNSSEC and rank movement for each. Those come from one probe per day at 11:11:11 UTC and do not move intraday. The nameservers and the points are read separately, at Cloudflare's recursive, and are refreshed throu

tools.name: dns_events
tools.description: Days when several resolvers were unhealthy at once, as episodes: when each began, how long it ran, how many resolvers were affected at the peak, and which. This is the tool for "was there a DNS outage recently".

tools.name: ksk_board
tools.description: The RFC 8509 root key sentinel across the public resolvers: which resolvers trust which root KSK, and the root DNSKEY set as read now.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_domain" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
